To what did you wish to look before
The window shut? To a place in heaven
Which I have lost,--to-day! No more there now;
I see it shining through the panes no more--
Never again, because my feet were turned
From where my heart was caught away from me.
And yet no tears, though near at hand, come down
Over that face which is so full of grief.

And the sun shines warm to-day;
But my heart is sad with longing today
For him who sings not here away.

O Beauty of Love! thy name is sweet;
Love has the same smile on every lip,
And in all hearts his will is complete
And what he wills to do that must be right.

The world is full of love so fair and true
That even I have felt it when I would,
Since first with eyes of rapture I could view
All human beauty from a woman’s side.

If ever I were free."

author: thomas_hardy
text:
WHEN LITTLE THOUGHTS ARE BEST

Little thoughts are best;
When little things we do,
To give us pleasure or to raise our brother's joy
Or help his labor through
The day of toil and pain
Is not an effort which a soul should say, "Nay!"

From 'little' deeds that grow
Into great ones done
Some mighty men have sprung, some ladies fair and queenly.
Who made the world with love
And thought of others more than self,
We know them by their power to make all hearts their own.

Men are but children of the Bough,
The sap of them runs all with blood;
They have no heads nor hands to move,
Nor feet beneath their bloody brood;
For every little thing they do
Is done in the way that I will show.

The men upon the Boughs above,
Who have a voice like women’s low,
And never have been seen or heard
Until we hear them singing loud;
Though when the world is very old,
They only live as people know.

Jessica has a new job at the corner store. She's wearing an old T-shirt and jeans, her hair is piled up on top of her head. Her hands are dirty with food from work.

Jessica walks in through the front door to find two men sitting on stools playing cards at the counter. A third man stands next to them. They all look tired and bored.

text: As I watched from the window of the blackness in the black van, we quickly craned down to see that iron gate bounce down the long lonely drive way lined with bare trees, to the abandoned house in the hills, where the grass was dead and the trees were dead. As the van stopped, Jessica ran out. I looked over my shoulder to see her run toward me screaming for help.

Her cat sat on the windowsill like a statue staring through the windowpane, and the walls were all covered in paintings of various kinds of animals.
